transcript.text:
Here's the full sequence of API calls to create a source and run an account aggregation.

---

## Step 1: Authenticate — Get an Access Token

Use the Client Credentials grant flow with your PAT's client ID and secret.

```bash
curl -X POST \
  'https://[tenant].api.identitynow.com/oauth/token' \
  --form 'grant_type="client_credentials"' \
  --form 'client_id="{your-client-id}"' \
  --form 'client_secret="{your-client-secret}"'
```

From the response, grab the `access_token`. All subsequent calls use it as `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`.

---

## Step 2: Create the Source

```bash
curl -X POST \
  'https://[tenant].api.identitynow.com/v3/sources' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "My New Source",
    "description": "Example source",
    "owner": {
      "type": "IDENTITY",
      "id": "{owner-identity-id}"
    },
    "connector": "active-directory",
    "connectorClass": "sailpoint.connector.ADLDAPConnector",
    "connectorAttributes": {
      "host": "ad.example.com",
      "port": "389",
      "baseDN": "DC=example,DC=com"
    }
  }'
```

Key fields to supply:
- `name` — required, unique display name
- `owner.id` — identity ID of the source owner (required)
- `connector` — connector type identifier (e.g., `active-directory`, `jdbc`, `webservices`)
- `connectorAttributes` — connector-specific connection settings (host, credentials, etc.)

The response body will include the new source's `id`. Save it — you need it for the next calls.

---

## Step 3: Verify the Source (Optional but Recommended)

Confirm the source was created and check its health before aggregating.

```bash
curl -X GET \
  'https://[tenant].api.identitynow.com/v3/sources/{sourceId}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}'
```

You can also run a connection test to make sure ISC can reach the source:

```bash
curl -X POST \
  'https://[tenant].api.identitynow.com/v3/sources/{sourceId}/check-connection' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}'
```

---

## Step 4: Trigger an Account Aggregation

Once the source is configured and connected, kick off an account aggregation:

```bash
curl -X POST \
  'https://[tenant].api.identitynow.com/v3/sources/{sourceId}/load-accounts' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: multipart/form-data'
```

For a flat-file (CSV) source, you'd attach the file:

```bash
curl -X POST \
  'https://[tenant].api.identitynow.com/v3/sources/{sourceId}/load-accounts' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/accounts.csv'
```

The response includes a task ID you can poll to monitor aggregation progress.

---

## Summary of the Flow

| # | Action | Method | Path |
|---|--------|--------|------|
| 1 | Get access token | POST | `/oauth/token` |
| 2 | Create source | POST | `/v3/sources` |
| 3 | Get source by ID | GET | `/v3/sources/{id}` |
| 4 | Test connection | POST | `/v3/sources/{id}/check-connection` |
| 5 | Run aggregation | POST | `/v3/sources/{id}/load-accounts` |

> **Note on permissions:** The JWT access token you use inherits the permissions of the PAT's generating user. That user must have admin or source admin rights to create sources and trigger aggregations.

```answer-summary

  - method: POST
    path: /oauth/token
    api_version: oauth
  - method: POST
    path: /v3/sources
    api_version: v3
  - method: GET
    path: /v3/sources/{id}
    api_version: v3
  - method: POST
    path: /v3/sources/{id}/check-connection
    api_version: v3
  - method: POST
    path: /v3/sources/{id}/load-accounts
    api_version: v3
auth_flow: OAuth2 bearer token (client credentials grant with PAT)
required_scopes: []
key_parameters: [name, owner, connector, connectorAttributes, sourceId, file]
```
